quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always be careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane. It warns you about a hazard ahead.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic around you.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match the freeway traffic. This helps you blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What will help someone recover from drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will allow alcohol to leave the body.

questions.question: When driving near children, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They will run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking first.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections, whether or not there is a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane will end. Drivers in the right lane must move to the left lane.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with blocked view, what is the maximum speed?
questions.correctAnswerText: 20 mph
questions.explanation: When you cannot see the railroad tracks clearly, drive no faster than 20 miles per hour.

questions.question: How do you properly enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal before merging and match the speed of freeway traffic. Always yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What should you do to merge into a busy freeway?

options.text: Check your side mirror, rearview mirror, and blind spots.
Speed up on the ramp to match freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Speed up on the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic and yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure you have room.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Highway signs that show dangerous road conditions are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to possible hazards ahead. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A driver can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left if there is an available passing lane. You may also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
There are a series of curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has three or more curves.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: May be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always use a proper car seat for children.

questions.question: At night, it is hardest to see:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: A bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws:

options.text: Is in the right because bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
You are entering a school's parking lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers that a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: What may help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in their driveways with their cars running.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel because you must accelerate again. Looking ahead and slowing down gradually or changing lanes helps you avoid hard braking and use less gas.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic control, you must yield to a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers don't see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When facing bright headlights at night, where should you look to reduce glare?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, focus on the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look at the headlights directly, as the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and use your turn signal. Look for other drivers moving into your lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
